claims.excerpt: ## Three Legislative Steps Toward the Interstate Highway System
claims.claim: Three legislative steps contributed to the development of the interstate highway system.
claims.label: F0 faithful
claims.evidence: The 1938 Federal-Aid Highway Act directed the Bureau of Public Roads chief to study a proposed six-route toll network. The 1944 Federal-Aid Highway Act authorized designating 40,000 miles for a national interstate network. The 1956 Act, dated June 29, authorized funding for highway construction and amended tax provisions for motor fuel, tires, trucks and buses. The National Archives identifies the 1956 law with establishing the interstate system.
claims.narrative: The development of the U.S. interstate highway system involved distinct legislative steps: studying a proposed six-route toll network, authorizing designation of a much larger national network, and later providing funding for highway construction.
claims.explanation: The title accurately summarizes the three legislative actions described in the source.
